text:
samir: Heads-up: onboarding 'cliff-0.9' embeddings in staging. FP16 baseline looks good, but after adding a whitening step we see a big recall@50 regression on our long-query cohort (drop ~0.12 absolute). Anyone seen whitening cause long-query collapse?

cleo: That's surprising. Whitening usually helps global structure. What exact whitening did you run (PCA-whiten, ZCA, regularized)?

samir: PCA-whiten with epsilon=1e-5 (sklearn: PCA(whiten=True)). Eval numbers: fp16 recall@50=0.902, whitened fp16=0.887, whitened+quant-int8=0.765. Long-query subset recall@50 went from 0.914 -> 0.782 after whitening+int8.

devin: Can you paste the eval command + index config? Also how do you split long vs short?

samir: Eval snippet: 
```
python eval/recall.py --model cliff-0.9 --holdout data/holdout_20k.csv --k 50 --cohort long --index hnsw --metric angular
```
Index config: HNSW ef_construction=200, ef_search=64, M=32. Long = queries with token_count > 60.

harper: Two immediate checks: 1) Are you L2-normalizing after whitening? Whitening breaks norm => need to renormalize before ANN. 2) Whitening can amplify low-variance directions which quant blows up.

samir: We renormalize after whitening. I think quant is the killer — the low-variance dims get huge scale changes and int8 clamping zeros them out. But even fp16 whitened has some drop (0.887).

cleo: Try ridge-regularized PCA (add small diag to covariance) or reduce whitening energy by keeping top-N components (like 0.99 explained variance). Also compare angular vs dot-product distances — whitening changes geometry.

devi n: (typo) I meant: try PCA with n_components=512 -> then renormalize. Also, what's the pre-whitened singular value spectrum look like? If it decays slowly, whitening is risky.

samir: Quick sv plot: top-10 sv: [45.2, 12.3, 6.1, 3.9, ...] long tail of tiny svs < 0.1 after comp 1024. So whitening massively upweights comps >1024 -> bad.

qa-bot: nightly-regression: cliff-0.9-whitened-int8 failed similarity-cohort-long: recall@50 delta -0.122 (alert sent). Link: https://ci.internal/alerts/cliff-202604

harper: Two options: A) PCA-truncate to keep variance threshold (0.999), B) use ZCA or sphere-projection instead of full whitening, C) apply per-dim clamp before quant (clip small dims). Also consider quantizing only top-k dims and storing tail as fp16 for ANN.

cleo: Reindexing thought: HNSW with angular probably interacts poorly — the renormalized but whitened vectors change pairwise angles. Try building index with dot-product (inner product) or increase ef_search to 128 as a quick hedge.

samir: I'll run three parallel experiments tonight: 1) PCA(whiten=False) + sphering (L2 only) 2) PCA-whiten but n_components=1024 (drop tiny sv comps) + int8 asymmetric per-channel 3) No whitening + post-hoc per-dim clipping + quant stochastic rounding. Scripts: 
```
./scripts/onboard_scan.sh --model cliff-0.9 --modes no-whiten,whiten-trunc,whiten-clipped --calib 50k --index-config ef_search=128
```
Run id: r-202604-cliff-whiten-scan-01

devin: Add a control: whitened fp16 with n_components=1024 (no quant) so we can separate whitening vs quant effects. Also export top-200 id-flips for the long cohort for manual inspection.

samir: Good call. I'll include fp16 controls and dump id-flip lists + 2D UMAP snapshots.

harper: If truncation helps, we can automate: compute cumulative explained variance, choose n where variance >= 0.995 for long-cohort embedding, maybe different n for different cohorts. Could be a dynamic preprocessing policy.

bench-bot: queued jobs: r-202604-cliff-whiten-scan-01 modes=[no-whiten,whiten-trunc,whiten-clipped] calib=50k index:ef_search=128. Expected finish ~AM PST. Results will be posted at https://ci.internal/bench/r-202604-cliff-whiten-scan-01

cleo: Also ping infra: if we need hybrid index (mixed precision storage) that's a slightly bigger infra lift but feasible for a canary. @ops please weigh in if we need storage changes.

samir: FYI I'll also run a quick cluster-purity sample: pick 100 long queries that lost top-1 neighbor after whitening and render top-5 neighbor text for product to eyeball UX impact. Will post samples here.

harper: One more: compute per-dim SNR on the calibration set and multiply whitening scales by a dampening factor (0 < alpha < 1) to avoid extreme reweighting. Try alpha in [0.2,0.5,0.8].

samir: Adding alpha sweep. Will report back with recall@10/50/100, silhouette, explained-variance, and a short list of id-flip clusters. Thanks all.
